A fresh scene of diplomatic rupture is unfolding in the heart of Europe , with Greece placing a veto on European Commission plans to further restrict the entry of Russian citizens into the Schengen area, as reported by Russian media outlet News.ru on September 4 . Specifically, several EU member states, including Spain , Greece , and Italy , oppose tightening entry conditions for Russians, reports the TASS news agency, citing a source close to Brussels . According to the source, multiple European countries do not support the blueprint proposed by Josep Borrell and Ursula von der Leyen , which envisions treating entry into the EU as a sort of... privilege for Russian citizens. At the same time, EU countries remain divided over the further tightening of visa policy for Russians. «This Brussels plan cannot be fully implemented due to countries that derive significant revenue from the tourism sector, such as Spain , Greece , and Italy », the source clarified. According to the same source, these countries have incurred notable economic losses following the severance of ties with Russia and are now compelled to rely on financial support from the EU budget. «We will not allow our tourism sector to be devastated...» Countries with developed tourism sectors, the source noted, do not wish to see this scenario expand further into their domestic economies. Concurrently, the source explained that the European Commission holds authority solely to provide legal advice to EU member states regarding visa policy, whereas decision-making in this domain remains within national competence. Substantive adjustments to Schengen visa issuance practices for nationals of a specific country, as noted, require a unanimous decision among EU member states. It is highlighted that on the other side of the Atlantic, US House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson expressed doubts that lawmakers will have time to review legislation tightening sanctions on Russia prior to November . According to the politician, the likelihood of putting the measure to a vote ahead of the congressional midterm elections on November 3 is exceptionally low. Greek intervention yields «softer» sanctions package against Russia It is recalled that in the summer of 2026 , European sanctions toward Russia softened for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Ukraine , amid a rift within the EU , as Greece and Italy pushed back firmly against the Brussels draft banning the entry of Russian military personnel into the Schengen area, as reported by Euractiv on July 10 . Consequently, the Commission abandoned the harshest clauses of the planned 21st sanctions package, European media outlets point out, citing diplomatic sources in Brussels . In Ukraine , these developments are received amid a manifest climate of panic, with Defense Minister of the Zelensky regime Andriy Sybiha openly expressing his «dissatisfaction» toward the European Commission , describing the package as «watered down». For the first time since 2022... a «milder» sanctions package The European Union was preparing to approve the 21st round of sanctions against Russia , but the restrictions turned out far milder than anticipated for the first time since 2022 , reports Euractiv . Severe disagreements surfaced among member states regarding visa issuance bans for Russian military personnel, restrictions on LNG exports, and the price cap on Russian oil. Extensive reporting across Russian and international media analyzed the rift that emerged over the sanctions the EU might adopt and why obstacles surround their passage. The European Commission abandoned the harshest provisions of the planned 21st sanctions package, reports Euractiv , citing diplomatic sources. According to the report, EU envoys were scheduled to agree on the new package on Friday July 10 , so foreign ministers could examine it during a meeting on Monday July 13 . Rift in the EU: Greece and Italy vetoed ban on Russian movement inside Schengen However, disagreements arose among EU states over multiple points, particularly concerning the entry ban for Russian military personnel into the EU . Initially, Estonia and Lithuania proposed a complete ban on visa issuance for active and former Russian military personnel. Nevertheless, according to Euractiv , France , Italy , and Greece opposed this wording. Representatives of other nations requested a more precise definition of the categories of individuals subject to restrictions, citing concerns that a blanket entry ban could prove technically unfeasible. The report claims that an outright ban is no longer under discussion. The measure was narrowed to short-stay visas, and the core criterion shifted to «active participation in hostilities or provision of assistance to military operations». According to the publication, the number of visas issued to Russian citizens by Schengen Area nations increased by 10.2% in 2025 compared to the previous year. France , Italy , and Spain issued the highest volume of visas to Russians. Disagreements also persist regarding restrictions on the Russian energy sector. Disagreements persist over Russian oil measures According to Euractiv , the European Commission proposed maintaining the price cap on Russian oil, which currently stands at 44 dollars per barrel. Under current EU rules, this metric is automatically adjusted every six months and must remain roughly 15% below the average market price. The next adjustment was scheduled for July 15 , reports Euronews . If the oil price cap were revised now, at a time when energy costs are elevated, the new cap could rise to around 58 dollars per barrel. In that scenario, over the subsequent six months (until the following revision), when oil prices decline, European firms would once again be able to transport and insure Russian fuel without the risk of violating the sanctions regime. The restriction would essentially no longer curtail Russian oil exports. This is why the European Commission proposed not revising the cap until January of next year and maintaining it at the current level of 44 dollars per barrel. However, Greece , as well as Cyprus and Malta (countries whose economies rely heavily on maritime transport), opposed the postponement and demanded that the freeze be reduced to three months instead of six. Maximos Mansion requests exemption for transport of Russian LNG outside the EU Greece also demanded other concessions that would enable it to supply Russian liquefied natural gas to non- EU countries. If accepted, Greece 's request would effectively dismantle the European Commission 's prohibition on the re-export of LNG to third nations, which is scheduled to take effect in January . At the same time, as Euractiv writes, consensus remains among EU countries on another European Commission proposal: prohibiting the sale of LNG tankers to Russia . According to Euractiv , member states are also discussing potential exemptions to import curbs on Russian fish. The publication notes that Germany seeks to retain the ability to purchase haddock, Poland cod, and Portugal bacalhau. https://www.dw.com/en/satirist-launches-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NTB0 The Chi Phi fraternity was barred from campus in 2024 Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Toby Morton, who wrote several episodes of the animated comedy series "South Park," launched a website seeking accountability in connection with an alleged 2024 sexual assault case involving seven fraternity members at Cornell University in the US . The site names seven men accused of sexually assaulting a 20-year-old woman who was allegedly unconscious after being given drugs and alcohol at a Cornell fraternity house, and collects personal data and photos of the members involved. "I've received messages reminding me I'm not a journalist, I'm 'just a satirist,'" Morton wrote in a September 27 Instagram post regarding the creation of his website TheCornell7.org. "This is true, but it makes me more dangerous," he added, saying he has "nobody to tell me I've gone too far." The case has recently drawn a surge in public attention after the accuser, identified as Jane Doe to protect her identity, filed a lawsuit in mid-September. Her complaint alleges that she was brutally sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity while unconscious after being pressured to take ketamine, smoke marijuana and drink alcohol at the fraternity house on Cornell's campus in Ithaca, New York. The university, she said in the lawsuit, failed to protect her. Cornell conducted an internal investigation after the incident, but no one was charged. The reopening of the case has caused renewed attention on social media Image: Heather Ainsworth/AP Photo/picture alliance Since the lawsuit was filed on September 16, the case has generated widespread commentary on social media. Some have criticized Cornell and the district attorney's office, while others have questioned the allegations. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who handled the original case, said his office has reopened it and plans to present evidence to a grand jury amid public questions about why no criminal charges were initially filed. Van Houten said in a statement that his office is considering bringing criminal charges related to the incident, though the allegations in the civil complaint are "dramatically different" from the woman's statement to police two years ago — in her statement to authorities, she did not allege she was drugged without her knowledge or that she did not consent to engage in sexual acts . Justice sought Cornell's Chi Phi chapter was barred from campus after the alleged incident in 2024. The woman who accused the men of sexual assault dropped out of Cornell University, according to her attorney. One of the most chilling allegations of the lawsuit is that a message was sent to a Chi Phi Snapchat group at about 1:42 a.m., inviting members to the room to abuse Doe, who was heavily under the influence of drugs and alcohol. The lawsuit alleges that more men then entered the room and that the assault continued for several hours until Doe lost consciousness. "There were so many people that could have prevented it and they didn't. I've never seen anything like it," an attorney for Jane Doe, Thomas Giuffra, told CBS. Giuffra pointed out that two of the seven accused fraternity members were expelled, while the others received lesser disciplinary measures. "Not one of these guys was arrested," Giuffra told the network. Actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as 'horrific' on social media Image: Cover Images/picture alliance Politicians and actors speak out Many people, from US politicians to Hollywood actors, have spoken out about the case in recent days. US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York Democrat, condemned what she described as a "culture of rape" protected by elite institutions. "When I read what happened at Cornell, those men posted in a group chat. That means it was normal to them. That means it was acceptable to them. This is a culture, and what we must do is understand that we cannot protect those spaces anymore," she said Sunday at a forum near Cornell's campus. British actress Florence Pugh described the allegations as "horrific" on social media and expressed her support for the student involved. Pugh, who is currently on a promotional tour for her upcoming Netflix series "East of Eden," wrote a lengthy statement on Instagram, saying that "Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world. You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won't be harmed in return." "Those who protect and impose light sentences on men who rape and destroy lives should be punished and closely scrutinized. Why are you protecting someone so fiercely?" she wrote. American actor Josh Gad, best known as the voice of Olaf in Disney's "Frozen" films, also commented on the Cornell case, criticizing what he described as insufficient disciplinary consequences for the students accused of sexual assault. In an Instagram post, Gad said sexual violence should not be treated as a mistake or addressed with limited disciplinary action by a university. He argued that the alleged conduct had "destroyed a life" and called for greater accountability. Edited by Joshua Lang. https://tibet.net/sikyong-penpa-tsering-.text: Sikyong Penpa Tsering to Visit Switzerland, Czech Republic and Germany; Will Attend Forum 2000 2 weeks ago Subscribe Post Views: 6,152 (File image) Sikyong Penpa Tsering to Visit Switzerland, Czech Republic and Germany; Will Attend Forum 2000 Dharamshala: Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) embarked on an official visit to three European countries earlier this morning and is scheduled to attend the upcoming Forum 2000 conference in Prague, Czech Republic. Over the next two days, Sikyong will undertake official engagements in Delhi before departing for Zurich, Switzerland, on 8 October. He is scheduled to hold a series of official engagements in Zurich on 9 and 10 October. On 11 October, Sikyong will depart for Prague, Czech Republic, where he will attend the Forum 2000 conference on 12 and 13 October. On 15 October, Sikyong will travel to Germany, where he is scheduled to undertake official engagements until 17 October, before returning to India. Sikyong is scheduled to arrive in Delhi on 19 October and will return to Dharamshala on 20 October. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/eu-c.text: The EU must turn its offer of “associate membership” to Canada into a meaningful partnership that goes well beyond trade, Tobias Cremer, the European Parliament's standing rapporteur on Canada, told Euronews.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen invited Canada to become the EU's first “associate member” in September, but gave little indication of what the unprecedented status would mean in practice.The offer comes as geopolitical upheaval draws Brussels and Ottawa closer together. Canada is embroiled in a trade war with its traditional US ally, while the EU is struggling to keep Washington on its side over Ukraine.The two sides are due to meet at a summit in Montreal at the end of next week, with agreements expected in several areas, including critical raw materials and digital cooperation.“For the last couple of months, we've been great, Canada and Europe, at writing each other love letters and saying how much we really want to work together,” said Cremer, a German socialist MEP. “But I think now is really the time to start to get serious and turn that love story into concrete commitments.”He added that “associate membership” must mean the “closest possible partnership that the EU can offer to a non-European country and since Canada is probably the most European of non-European countries that should be very close.”Beyond trade dealsCremer insisted that the relationship must amount to more than “a trade deal ‘plus’”.“There must be a new quality to the relation.”He called for a “pragmatic approach,” involving sectoral agreements covering trade, defence, digital cooperation, the Arctic and students, but also going further.“We should go a step further and start embedding all of these great initiatives into something more enduring, into a common institutional framework of coordination and cooperation.”Cremer suggested that Canada could participate “as an observer” in the Council of the EU, where national ministers meet, and called for the creation of a formal parliamentary partnership assembly.Such a body could follow the model of the existing EU-UK Parliamentary Partnership Assembly, which brings together 35 members from each side twice a year for sessions that can focus on specific policy areas.Regarding the UK, however, the MEP described it as a European country for which, “if it wishes so,” the ambition “should not be associate membership, but full membership.”His comments came as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently floated the idea of rejoining the EU, with polls showing that a majority of Britons want to return to the bloc.But Cremer also argued for closer cooperation not only with the UK and Canada, but also with countries such as Australia and South Korea.“I think it is of our interest to bring all of these actors together and say 'hold on, actually the majority of the world wants to play 21st century politics which is focused on collective security, on shared interests, on mutual respect rather than might is right.'”
